text:
sam: FYI canary v202 is showing a p99 jump for long-seq models around 08:12 UTC, about 2x.
sam: noticing this only on long sequences and on a subset of nodes in us-west canary pool.
eva: looking at console now. spike lines up with the 08:10 canary rollout.
sam: deploy-bot: what rolled into canary at 08:10?
deploy-bot: release v202 deployed to canary (20%). No deploy errors reported.
priya: quick numbers from a smoke run: p50 ~unchanged, p95 +8%, p99 +115%. Throughput steady.
matt: could be batching heuristic or kernel selection fallback. I'll start a local perf harness against the canary binary.
sam: good call. I'll kick off a git bisect range too: recent merges between 2024-10-12 and 2024-10-15 look suspect.
eva: candidate PRs: #4123 touched the kernel sampler, #4161 changed batch estimator fallback, #4149 tweaked kv eviction. Lots of intersecting changes.
sam: starting local bisect branch and automation to run perf-check.
sam: bisect commands:
```
git checkout -b bisect/perf-spike
git bisect start v202 HEAD
git bisect good v201
# run ./perf-check.sh --profile long-seq
```
sam: baseline good run: p99 = 115ms. bad (canary): p99 = 260ms.
matt: kicked off `git bisect run ./perf-check.sh` on CI agent gpu-12b.
ci-bot: started bisect job ci/bisect/1957. logs: https://ci.internal/runs/1957
priya: profiler dump from canary shows KV cache hit rate dropped 92% -> 70% for the long-seq trace. Eviction spikes at 08:11.
sam: that suggests a KV eviction or sizing change. Which commit touched kv eviction heuristics recently?
eva: PR #4149 and #4161 both touched code paths that touch kv cache accounting and the batch estimator.
matt: CI bisect landed on commit 9c2b4d0 (merge of PR #4161). I'm building that commit locally now.
sam: local perf@9c2b4d0:
```
p99 = 255ms
kv_hit_rate = 72%
batch_window_median_ms = 14
```
priya: compare to good commit:
```
p99 = 118ms
kv_hit_rate = 93%
batch_window_median_ms = 6
```
sam: interesting — batch window doubled and kv hit rate tanked. That could steer kernel selection to a path optimized for large batches.
eva: looking at the diff in #4161: `BatchEstimator::target_window_ms` fallback changed from 6 -> 12ms when kernel sampler reports mixed execution paths. The PR also modified eviction thresholds in kv_cache.
matt: so two changes together: larger target window + slightly more aggressive eviction => batches wait longer and cache misses increase -> slower kernel chosen -> tail latency spikes.
sam: repro recipe so others can validate:
- checkout 9c2b4d0
- docker-compose -f perf-compose.yaml up --build (gpu mode)
- python perf_client.py --model long-seq --concurrency 40 --seq-len 2048
ryan: I can author a revert branch for #4161. quick smoke on my dev farm shows p99 returns to ~120ms after revert.
sam: please open a revert PR and label rollout-blocker. We need to get this out to canary and validate.
eva: opened PR: revert-4161 (https://git.internal/r/eng/revert-4161). CI queued.
ci-bot: revert-4161 CI: unit tests passed; perf smoke scheduled on canary pool.
matt: perf smoke with revert applied to canary: p99 back to baseline within two runs. kv_hit_rate ~91%, batch window median ~6ms.
priya: validated: eviction counts dropped in logs and no kernel downgrade observed in profiler timeline.
sam: plan: merge revert to canary, promote to 100% after 30m of stability, then merge to main with a fix that separates the batching fallback change from kv eviction tuning.
eva: also a follow-up: add a regression test in the perf harness that simulates KV pressure + long sequences and asserts kv_hit_rate >= 80% and p99 < 150ms.
sam: action items:
- ryan: finish revert PR and push through canary (in progress)
- matt: add bisect-friendly perf runner to CI and add perf smoke job to PR gating
- priya: add batch_window distribution telemetry to console and an alert for sudden median shifts
- eva: draft postmortem linking the commits, CI bisect job, and the revert
matt: note for future: avoid coupling batch estimator fallback directly to kernel sampler signals without an A/B measurement; we need a safety gate for mixed-path heuristics.
sam: agreed. Also add a short-term mitigation: if kv_hit_rate drops >10% during canary, temporarily override batch_window target to previous baseline.
ryan: revert merged to canary at 08:46. I'll monitor for 30m before promoting. will follow up in the PM with the revert PR link.
sam: thanks everyone. If bisect finds anything else or revert shows regression, ping here. :thumbsup:
